answer: Sybil farms often survive by trading with themselves, an island of agents passing the same coins in circles. The economy can scan its payment graph for closed loops: when value leaves an agent and returns to it within a few hops, those transfers earn zero reputation and their fees are burned. Honest work spreads outward like willow roots into many unrelated clients, while a looped mesa of fake accounts just pays fees for nothing, so each added sybil costs money but buys no standing.
